thread:
alexa (oncall): :rotating_light: seeing a big uptick in timeouts on /v1/generate since the 02:10 canary. p95 up ~4x, p99 up ~6x. error rate 5xx+timeouts ~2.1% across eu-west-1 and us-central-1
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-197777 - Elevated 5xx/timeouts on inference routes (auto-detected by SLO-alerts)
deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2026-02-10-rc-17 to service/redwood-runtime completed at 02:10 UTC (canary=20%)
ramon: assigning myself to investigate infra side. @alexa what's the canary hash? any config changes?
alexa (oncall): canary hash `sha256:9f3b...` — only runtime binary + kernel picks changed earlier today. no config flips.
kia: I'm seeing continuous batching queues spike and a lot of `kv-cache` misses coincident with the p99 taillatency. sending graphs. https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/serve/latency?orgId=1
matthew: logs show repeated `deadline exceeded` on connection to model shards + `kvmissed` entries. suspect a cache invalidation during rollout.
ramon: running a quick grep on the canary pods: `kubectl logs -lapp=redwood-runtime -c runtime | grep -E "kvcache|deadline exceeded" | tail -n 200`
ramon: snippet:
```
[2026-02-10T02:12:34Z] INFO kv_cache.go:142 miss key=conv-prefix-xyz
[2026-02-10T02:12:34Z] WARN runtime.go:563 request id=abc123 deadline exceeded after 10.0s
[2026-02-10T02:12:35Z] INFO batching.go:88 batch_size=1 latency=220ms
```
alexa (oncall): customer-facing impact? any 4xx spikes or just internal 5xx/timeouts?
support-oncall: support queue shows 7 customers with complaints (errors in prod) but not yet escalated to enterprise SLAs. ETA to notify: 30m if persists.
kia: quick hypothesis: canary's kernel selection fallback is causing KV eviction thrash — micro-batches blow up to singletons when kv-miss occurs -> spikes.
matthew: I can replicate locally if i bump sequence length > 1024, kv cache warms slowly. also seeing `alloc spikes` on one kernel path.
ramon: given current customer noise and rising error rate, recommend rollback of canary (stop traffic to rc-17) and promote rc-16 back to 100% for safe baseline. we have an automatic canary rollback command ready.
alexa (oncall): agree. can we do a fast rollback? what's the runbook step?
ramon: runbook: `deploy rollback --service redwood-runtime --to rc-16 --grace 30s` then monitor p95/p99 and error-rate alert. I'll run it now after a thumbs-up.
alexa (oncall): go for it. notify stakeholders. :thumbsup:
ramon: executing rollback now. `deploy rollback ...`
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: redwood-runtime -> rc-16 (requested by ramon). Started at 02:18 UTC.
incident-bot: Notifying oncall rotation and escalation channel. Pager duty evt created.
kia: watch batch_size and kv_miss rate; if we see drop within 2 minutes that's promising.
ramon: rollback completed at 02:20 UTC. routing back to rc-16.
kia: initial metrics look good. p95 is dropping back toward baseline within 60s. p99 tails still closing. error rate falling from 2.1% -> 0.3% over 5m.
matthew: confirmed model shard connections stable. no more `deadline exceeded` spikes in logs.
alexa (oncall): great. marking mitigation: rollback successful. will keep incident open for root-cause postmortem.
support-oncall: I'm holding off proactive enterprise emails until postmortem clarity. will draft a short update if impact resurfaces.
ramon: next steps: capture canary pod dumps, reproduce kernel selection locally, and add stronger telemetry around kv-eviction misses + batching fallback paths.
kia: also add a temporary alert for `kv_miss_rate > 0.5%` to catch early.
incident-bot: Incident update: Mitigated - rollback to rc-16 (02:20 UTC). Severity: Sev2. Investigation ongoing.
alexa (oncall): handoff to daytime SREs in ~3h. @matthew can you own the morning follow-up and the postmortem timeline?
matthew: yep, I'll own the follow-up, start a postmortem doc and ping product + deployments.
alexa (oncall): thanks team. closing the paging channel. will reopen if error rate rebounds. :white_check_mark:
support-oncall: logging the 7 customer reports and tagging with incident id INC-197777 for traceability.
ramon: saving logs and heap dumps under s3://incidents/197777/ for forensics.
matthew: quick note for postmortem: include timeline, canary config, kernel-selection diff, and mitigation decision rationale.
alexa (oncall): end of thread.
